Fuel longer rucks

Prepare food, water and resupply before the event.

Endurance · 4 min read · Updated 2026-11-24

Plan for time outside

A longer event is not simply a shorter session repeated. Think about the expected time, weather, elevation and available stops. Carry enough water for the route and know where refills are possible; avoid assuming every water source is usable.

Test your food

Choose foods you can tolerate while moving. Practise eating and drinking during manageable training sessions, rather than trying new products on event day. Plan a spare option and adapt to your own needs.

Finish ready for the next session

After the ruck, drink and eat according to your needs, check your feet and change out of wet clothing. For multi-day events, plan recovery in advance. If you have specific dietary or health needs, seek individual advice.

Rehearse the event plan

For a longer outing, identify reliable water refill points and decide when you can pause to eat. Bring food you already tolerate and a backup if the route takes longer. Log what you actually consumed and how comfortable it was. Use those observations for the next session instead of adopting a universal intake target. Check organiser rules on support stations and outside assistance.

Build a food and water plan you can repeat

Estimate how long you will be out, find the actual refill options and pack a fallback. Test small portions of familiar food on training days. Keep a simple record of what you ate and drank, when you stopped and whether anything upset your stomach. Long events and hot conditions change the requirements. Do not force a fixed water target; use individual guidance if you have health needs.

Further reading

  • Thomas, Erdman and Burke (2016): Nutrition and Athletic Performance — Joint sports nutrition position statement; applies across different training and competition demands.
